body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 5bbd29c1e09f49358337d78be14c917b5aca1d49 -->
Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.

**What looks good**
- The band region is a pure intersection. `boundary::resolve` clips the area to the lane (`boundary.rs`, new `area.intersect(l)`). The clip can only make the area smaller. No gouge check, collision check or section law is changed or skipped.
- The hook runs only with no tilted frame (`boundary_ctx.rs`). A tilted plane keeps the old refusal.
- Unclear selections are refused by name (`open_band.rs`). One open edge keeps the old refusal word for word (`open_band::mid_edge`).
- The new code has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`. The division in the touch check uses `.max(1e-24)`.
- The test `a_band_pass_that_cuts_another_part_blocks_the_post` shows that a band pass that cuts a kept part blocks the post.
- No golden file and no snapshot PNG changed. The decision record is present. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1735`. No dependency, no process file, no `build.rs` change.
- The new module has a provenance line. `open_band.rs` has 388 lines, within the limit.

**Merge commit 7381d9e55 (hand-resolved conflict)**
I read `git show --remerge-diff`. The conflict was only in `stitch.rs`, on `gather_runs`. The result keeps main's `setup: Option<&str>` parameter and the `OpFrame::new(setup...)` line. It adds `pub(super)`. In `open_band.rs`, `gather_runs(world, setup, items, None)` and (in the last commit) `stitch_open_runs(world, setup, items, None)` pass the setup. Main's setup-frame pose is kept. The diff of `stitch.rs` against main is one word: `pub(super)`.

**Results (locally, Windows, merged with main as of the fetch; main was not moved in the trial)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test open_band`: 7 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib open_band`: 3 passed.
- Neighbour suites, all green: area_open, slot_pick_refusals, slot_picks, stitch_cross, area_picks, opframe_picks, narrow_band, slot_extension, pick_doors, pick_agnostic, refusal_location.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- I did not run the whole quick plan (it is 190 app suites and 6 ui suites because the gate map names `app::operation`). I ran only the suites that cover picks and the open edge.
- Mutation check: I removed the lane clip in `boundary.rs`. `the_extension_moves_the_open_ends_out_of_the_stock_along_the_walls` failed, as it must. The other six tests still passed (the extension-0 case is bounded by the part law and the stock anyway). The mutation was reverted.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The lane clip is pinned by one test only (the extension test). A second test that sets the clip alone as the limit (a case where the part law does not already bound the area) would make the pin stronger.
2. The body says the quick gate was not run on the final head. This review ran the touched suites on the merged head, as listed above.
3. Not exercised by anyone: curved walls, a STEP tessellation, a tilted setup, Linux and macOS.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
